title: Thanksgiving Storm Knocks Out Power for Hundreds of Thousands, Postpones Macy's Parade as Black Friday Spending Hits Record Pace

content:
A powerful storm swept across much of the East Coast and the Midwest on Thanksgiving Day, knocking out power for hundreds of thousands of people, flooding coastal streets, canceling hundreds of flights and forcing the postponement of the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York.

Flooding caused most of the damage and disruption, NPR reported. Several bridges in New Jersey were shut down, and people were seen kayaking through usually busy streets in parts of coastal Virginia. Exceptionally high tides, known as King Tides, battered the West Coast at the same time. Some reports put the number of customers without power at close to one million.

The storm hit during one of the busiest travel periods of the year. Hundreds of flights were canceled and thousands delayed as travelers tried to get home for the holiday. Forecasters expected the storms to move out and the tides to recede heading into Saturday, as people began their journeys home.

For Laredo readers with family flying in or out for the holiday weekend, the delays rippled through the national air system even though South Texas stayed clear of the storm itself.

Meanwhile, Black Friday arrived with a twist: despite inflation and worries about the cost of living, Americans are expected to spend a record amount again this year. The National Retail Federation predicts a 4.2 percent increase in holiday retail sales compared with last year. Surveys show shoppers cutting back on other spending to afford the holidays, putting more essentials in their carts alongside gifts, and leaning on AI tools to find deals — even as more shoppers choose to buy in person this year.

Sources: NPR / Up First, Nov. 27, 2026; Associated Press; National Retail Federation.
